To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the error detection probability for 1’s complement and 2’s compression algorithm in wireless sensor networks is a function of the number of errors, and the probability decreases as the number of errors increases; the error detection probability decreases as the packet length increases, and the probability increases as the packet length decreases.

1) 1’s complement error passing probability can be expressed by a formula; the probability is a decreasing function and the probability is higher than the 2’s complement one for the same error pattern; 2) the existing header compression algorithms do not work well in wireless sensor networks; and 3) the adaptive header compression algorithm is more suitable for wireless sensor networks.
• We propose a new method to calculate the probability of error passing for 1’s complement.
